title: RAG Security and ACLs
tagline: The model can only leak what retrieval hands it.
story: The question has been embedded, matched and ranked, and a set of chunks is about to enter the prompt. Some chunks belong to people who should never see them, and some contain instructions written by strangers. Here you decide who enforces access, where, and how you prove it still holds after a permission changes.
oneLiner: Enforce access in retrieval with the caller's identity, treat every retrieved word as hostile, and test revocation like a feature.
youWillLearn: Map RAG threats to OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 and MITRE ATLAS ids and name the stage where each one lands
Layer defences against indirect injection, poisoning and exfiltration, and know which layers are probabilistic
Resolve who is asking: on-behalf-of, groups claim overage, nested groups and least-privilege retrieval identities
Choose among post-filter, pre-filter, live check, delegation to the source and physical walls by flipping the dials
Use the ACL simulator to see recall collapse, empty answers and revocation leakage as numbers
Pick among the four Azure AI Search document-level approaches and say what is GA and what is preview
Keep permissions true over time: sync, drift audits, revocation tests, cache scoping and log hygiene
Defend an access control design and run the response to a reported leak

flashcards.front: Which OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 id covers cross-tenant leaks in shared vector stores and embedding inversion?
flashcards.back: LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses. Mitigations include permission-aware vector stores with strict logical and access partitioning, data validation and immutable retrieval logs.

flashcards.front: Why is the model never the authorization layer?
flashcards.back: A prompt rule is probabilistic and the denied text is already in the context. Enforce access in retrieval and tools, using the caller's identity.

flashcards.front: Name the three legs of the Agents Rule of Two.
flashcards.back: Untrustworthy input, access to sensitive systems or private data, and the ability to change state or communicate externally. Keep at most two per session, or add human approval.

flashcards.front: What did the EchoLeak chain (CVE-2025-32711) combine?
flashcards.back: A classifier bypass, reference-style Markdown that evaded link redaction, auto-fetched images and an allowed Teams proxy. One crafted email, zero clicks.

flashcards.front: PoisonedRAG headline result?
flashcards.back: About 90% attack success with five malicious texts per target question, injected into a knowledge base of millions of texts. The tested defences were insufficient.

flashcards.front: Name the three spotlighting modes.
flashcards.back: Delimiting with randomized delimiters, datamarking with a token woven through untrusted text, and encoding such as base64. Probabilistic: attack success fell from above 50% to below 2% in the paper.

flashcards.front: Post-filter over-fetch formula, and what it hides?
flashcards.back: k_fetch = k_needed / visible_fraction. At 2% visible and 10 wanted, fetch 500. It also leaks if denied text reaches rerankers, logs or caches before the filter runs.

flashcards.front: Why does a pre-filter keep top-k full, and what does it cost?
flashcards.back: The filter runs inside the nearest-neighbour search, so only allowed documents compete. ANN recall can degrade under a very selective filter, so measure recall at your real selectivity.

flashcards.front: When does a live source check beat index ACLs?
flashcards.back: When revocation must be near immediate or the rules are richer than an index field can hold (deny, sharing links, guests). Cost: latency and source load, so check only the top hits.

flashcards.front: Entra token group limits and what replaces the claim above them?
flashcards.back: JWT 200, SAML 150, implicit flow 6. Above that the groups claim becomes an overage indicator (`hasgroups` or `_claim_names`). Call Graph `transitiveMemberOf` for the list.

flashcards.front: What does the on-behalf-of flow guarantee?
flashcards.back: The middle tier exchanges the caller's token for a downstream token using delegated scopes only, so the downstream service sees the user and not a broad service account.

flashcards.front: How does Azure AI Search native ACL enforcement learn who is asking?
flashcards.back: The `x-ms-query-source-authorization` header carries the user's Entra token. A document passes if userIds, groupIds or rbacScope matches. Preview as of 2026-10-13.

flashcards.front: What changed in `2025-11-01-preview` for native ACL queries with no user token?
flashcards.back: ACL filters apply even with an API key or admin role, and a missing token returns only public (`all`) documents. Earlier previews returned everything.

flashcards.front: Limits on native ACL permission fields?
flashcards.back: One field per permission type per index, 1,000 values per userIds or groupIds field, five distinct rbacScope values. Use Entra object ids, not UPNs or emails.

flashcards.front: What is the revocation floor for a pull-built index?
flashcards.back: The indexer schedule interval has a 5 minute minimum (maximum 1,440). Push ingestion can merge ACL changes immediately, but you then own the change feed.

flashcards.front: How do you scope an Azure API Management semantic cache safely?
flashcards.back: Partition with `vary-by` on user or group id, keep `score-threshold` strict (docs suggest starting near 0.05, above 0.2 may mismatch) and set a TTL below the revocation SLA.

flashcards.front: What should a permissioned RAG system log by default?
flashcards.back: Identifiers and decision inputs: document ids, principal id, filter hash, outcome. Content copies protected text into a store without ACLs, so capture it only for a bounded, access-controlled window.

flashcards.front: A SharePoint parent permission changes. Does the AI Search indexer pick it up?
flashcards.back: Not per run. Item-level unique ACL changes sync each run from `2026-05-01-preview`; parent scope changes need `/resync` with `options: ["permissions"]` or `/resetdocs`.

flashcards.front: What silently disables filtering on an indexed knowledge source?
flashcards.back: Creating it without `ingestionPermissionOptions`. The index then has no permission metadata and results come back unfiltered whatever the header says. The option is still preview in the 2026-04-01 API.

flashcards.front: Does `retrievable: false` on an ACL field secure it?
flashcards.back: No. It hides the field from responses only. The filter on the field is the control, and the principal in the filter is only a string until your code derives it from a validated token.

glossary.def: Access control list. The principals (users, groups, roles) allowed to read one document, stored with the document or its chunks.
Removing results the caller may not see. Where it runs (in the index, in your code or at the source) is the main design choice.
A permission filter applied inside the vector or hybrid search, so only allowed documents compete for the top k.
A permission check applied after retrieval. Cheap to build, but it wastes top k and lets denied text reach later stages.
The share of the corpus a caller may see. Low values starve post-filters and stress filtered ANN recall.
When a user has more groups than a token can hold (200 for JWT), the token carries an overage indicator instead of the list, and you call Microsoft Graph.
An OAuth flow where a middle tier trades the caller's token for a downstream token with delegated scopes, preserving the user's identity.
A service with broad access that acts for a caller without proving the caller's rights, so the caller gains access they do not hold.
Instructions hidden in data the model retrieves, such as a page, email or file, rather than typed by the user.
Marking untrusted text (delimiting, datamarking or encoding) so the model can tell data from instructions. Probabilistic.
A design heuristic: one agent session should hold at most two of untrusted input, sensitive access, and state change or external communication.
The agreed time between removing access at the source and the last place that honours it (index, caches, tokens, logs) stopping. A choice per sensitivity tier, not a vendor number.
Mismatch between the ACL in the index and the ACL at the source, caused by missed events, inherited changes or failed syncs.
A planted document with a known ACL used to prove that filters, caches and logs behave, for example that a revoked test user never sees it.
On an error such as a Graph outage, return no restricted results (or an error) instead of unfiltered results.
An explicit admin request that bypasses ACL filters for debugging in Azure AI Search, sent as the header `x-ms-enable-elevated-read: true`.

claims.text: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 lists LLM01 Prompt Injection, LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure, LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning, LLM05 Improper Output Handling, LLM06 Excessive Agency and LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses.

OWASP LLM08 names unauthorized access, cross-context leaks in multi-tenant vector stores, embedding inversion and poisoning, and recommends permission-aware vector stores and immutable retrieval logs.
The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 was published on 2025-12-09 and runs from ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack to ASI10 Rogue Agents.
MITRE ATLAS (release 2026.09) has AML.T0070 RAG Poisoning, AML.T0071 False RAG Entry Injection, AML.T0051.001 indirect prompt injection and AML.T0086 Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation.
Greshake et al. (arXiv 2302.12173) was submitted on 2023-02-23 and describes indirect prompt injection against LLM-integrated applications.

EchoLeak is CVE-2025-32711, scored 9.3 by Microsoft and 7.5 by NVD, with an NVD record published on 2025-06-11 and CWE-74. The chain combined an XPIA classifier bypass, reference-style Markdown that evaded link redaction, auto-fetched images and an allowed Teams proxy.
PoisonedRAG reported about 90% attack success with five malicious texts per target question in a knowledge base of millions of texts.
Spotlighting reduced attack success from above 50% to below 2% on GPT-family models in the authors' experiments, using delimiting, datamarking or encoding.
CaMeL solved 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security versus 84% for an undefended agent.

Meta's Agents Rule of Two (2025-10-31) says one session should hold no more than two of untrustworthy input, access to sensitive systems or private data, and the ability to change state or communicate externally.
An Entra token carries at most 200 groups for JWT, 150 for SAML and 6 for the implicit flow. Above that an overage indicator replaces the groups claim.
Microsoft Graph transitiveMemberOf returns 100 items per page by default and 999 at most, and advanced queries need the header ConsistencyLevel: eventual.
The on-behalf-of flow uses delegated scopes only, and a middle tier must return 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header when the downstream API requires Conditional Access such as MFA.
Microsoft 365 Copilot Retrieval API limits are 200 requests per user per hour, 25 results at most and results are unordered. Pay-as-you-go consumption is preview.
Azure AI Search maximum indexes per service are Basic 15, S1 50, S2 and S3 200, and S3 HD 1,000 per partition or 3,000 per service.
Pinecone allows 100 (Starter) to 1,000,000 (Enterprise) namespaces per serverless index, and Cosmos DB logical partitions are limited to 20 GB.
The API Management llm-semantic-cache-lookup policy uses score-threshold with a suggested start near 0.05, mismatches may occur above 0.2, and vary-by partitions the cache.
A 2025 audit (ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.07776) detected global prompt cache sharing across users in seven API providers and showed timing differences can leak prompts.
Azure OpenAI prompt caches are not shared between Azure subscriptions.

Azure AI Search lists four document-level approaches: security filters (any API version), POSIX-like ACL and RBAC scopes, Purview sensitivity labels and SharePoint ACLs. The last three are preview as of 2026-10-13.
Purview label ingestion in Azure AI Search needs a system-assigned managed identity, is single tenant, and disables Autocomplete and Suggest on the index.

Native ACL queries pass the user's Entra token in the header x-ms-query-source-authorization. A document passes if any of userIds, groupIds or rbacScope matches, groups resolve through Microsoft Graph at query time, and a Graph failure returns 5xx instead of a partial result.
From 2025-11-01-preview ACL filters apply even with an API key or admin role, and a missing user token returns only public documents. Earlier previews returned all documents.
Elevated read uses the header x-ms-enable-elevated-read: true, works on Search POST but not knowledge base retrieve, and needs Search Index Data Contributor or a role with elevatedOperations/read.

Native permission fields: one field per permissionFilter type per index, at most 1,000 values in a userIds or groupIds field and at most five distinct rbacScope values. Use Entra object ids, not UPNs.

The SharePoint indexer does not support Anyone or People in your organization links, guests or Information Management policies, does not expand an Entra group nested in a SharePoint group, and needs /resync with options ["permissions"] for parent scope changes.
The latest stable Azure AI Search data-plane API is 2026-04-01 and the latest preview is 2026-08-01-preview. Knowledge sources are GA but ingestionPermissionOptions stays preview.
Azure AI Search ACL entry limits are 32 per ADLS Gen2 file or directory and 1,000 per SharePoint file, and entries beyond the limit might not be enforced.
The Azure AI Search indexer schedule interval is 5 minutes at minimum and 1,440 minutes at maximum.
Graph subscriptions on directory resources last at most 41,760 minutes, and driveItem notification latency is under 1 minute on average and 6 hours at most.
